rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase بعضهم من بعض expresses a shared relation: believers are allies, while the comparison with 3:34 evokes common lineage; the cited disbelievers instead disavow one another.
rows.anchor: المؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “some of you are from others” means people intermingle and ally with one another under Islam’s outward legal ruling.
rows.anchor: أي بعضكم يلابس بعضا ويواليه في ظاهر الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مع means accompaniment between two matters sharing an action or ruling; its complete sense is shared participation in the matter, not necessarily simultaneity. In 12:36 it marks the youths entering prison alongside Joseph.
rows.anchor: وكمال معنى المعية الاجتماع في الأمر الذي به الاشتراك دون زمانه فالأول يكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In abstract or inward actions, مع marks sharing a quality, belief, or state, as in worship, truthfulness, and the prophets’ shared divine support.
rows.anchor: والثاني يكثر في الأفعال المعنوية نحو آمنت مع المؤمنين وتبت مع التائبين وفهمت المسألة مع من فهمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s being “with us” in this verse means His care and protection.
rows.anchor: لا تحزن إن الله معنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described as believing with the Prophet are the people who shared his faith, the quality in which they were joined.
rows.anchor: يوم لا يخزي الله النبي والذين آمنوا معه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reading takes معه as temporal accompaniment: the light was revealed with the Prophet’s mission or with his following, with an omitted noun understood.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه من باب المعية في الاشتراك فتمامه الاجتماع في الزمان على حذف مضاف إما أن يكون تقديره أنزل مع نبوته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading makes معه express participation in the shared matter rather than time, effectively “follow the light along with him.”
rows.anchor: وقيل لأنه فيما وقع به الاشتراك دون الزمان وتقديره واتبعوا معه النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes ما as a relative pronoun, with آمنتم به as its relative clause: believe in what you believe in.
rows.anchor: وجوابه ان تكون ما موصولة صلتها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative treats ما as redundant, yielding belief in what the Muslims believe in: God, angels, books, messengers, and all prophetic revelation.
rows.anchor: وقيل مزيدة والتقدير فان آمنوا بالذي آمنتم به اي بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله وجميع ما جاء به الانبياء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third proposal makes مثلا an adjective of an omitted noun (“something like what you believe”); the author objects that what they believe has no like to believe in.
rows.anchor: وقيل ان مثلا صفة لمحذوف تقديره فان آمنوا بشيء مثل ما آمنتم به وفيه نظر لان ما أمنوا به ليس له مثل

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi transmits from most commentators that “the face” is an extra expression here, so the sense is that God is present, knowing and seeing.
rows.anchor: ان الوجه صلة والمعنى فثم الله يعلم ويرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers taking “face” to mean God’s essence, as in other verses, over claiming the word is redundant.
rows.anchor: قلت والاشبه حمله على ان المراد به الذات

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda treats إذ in “Do they hear you when you call?” as an extra particle.
rows.anchor: ومن الزيادة دعوى أبا عبيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They will beget only a wicked, unbelieving child” names the child by what he will become.
rows.anchor: اي صائرا إلى الفجور والكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dreamer calls it bread although birds eat grain, because grain is what the bread will become; the author says scholars usually cite only the wine example.
rows.anchor: أي لأن الذي تأكل الطير منه إنما هو البر لا الخبز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I am pressing wine” means grapes, named for the wine they will become.
rows.anchor: أي عنبا فعبر عنه لأنه آيل إلى الخمرية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view denies metaphor because خمر is itself a lexical name for grapes in the language of Azd Oman; al-Farisi reports this from Ibn Durayd.
rows.anchor: نقله الفارسي في التذكرة عن غريب القرآن لابن دريد

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the wording as naming the cause (grapes) by its effect (wine).
rows.anchor: وقيل اكتفى بالمسبب الذي هو الخمر عن السبب الذي هو العنب قاله ابن جني في الخصائص

rows.speaker: ابن عزيز
rows.claim: Ibn Aziz locates the figurative usage in the verb أعصر, which means “extract,” rather than in the noun خمر.
rows.anchor: واليه ذهب ابن عزيز في غريبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second husband is called a spouse because the marriage contract will make him one; at the moment of the new marriage, he is not yet her husband.
rows.anchor: سماه زوجا لان العقد يئول إلى زوجية

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: The beginning-of-revelation report in al-Bukhari, explicitly authenticated by al-Hakim from Aisha, establishes اقرأ as the first revelation; Muslim gives it through “He taught man what he did not know.”
rows.anchor: وأخرجه الحاكم فى مستدركه من حديث عائشة رضى الله عنها صريحا وقال صحيح الإسناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim’s wording extends the first revelation through “He taught man what he did not know”; al-Bukhari’s version stops at “your Lord is most generous,” which the author calls an accepted abridgment.
rows.anchor: ولفظ مسلم أول ما نزل من القرآن

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports in Sahih Muslim that al-Muddaththir was the first revelation, apparently conflicting with the Aisha report.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء ما يعارض هذا ففى صحيح مسلم عن جابر أول ما نزل من القرآن سورة المدثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reconciles Jabir’s report by saying he heard only the end of the Prophet’s account of the first revelation and mistook al-Muddaththir, revealed after the pause, for the absolute beginning.
rows.anchor: وجمع بعضهم بينهما بأن جابرا سمع النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم يذكر قصة بدء الوحى فسمع آخرها ولم يسمع أولها فتوهم أنها أول ما نزلت

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: The two Ṣaḥīḥ collections report Jabir’s account: after the pause, the Prophet saw the angel again between heaven and earth, returned frightened asking to be covered, and then received al-Muddaththir.
rows.anchor: لما ثبت فى الصحيحين أيضا عن جابر رضى الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يحدث عن فترة الوحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken together, the reports show that اقرأ was the first revelation absolutely and al-Muddaththir followed it after the pause.
rows.anchor: فقد أخبر فى هذا الحديث عن الملك الذى جاءه بحراء قبل هذه المرة

rows.speaker: ابن حيان
rows.claim: Ibn Hibban likewise sees no conflict: اقرأ came at Hira, then after the Prophet returned to Khadija, al-Muddaththir was revealed in her house.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قال ابن حيان فى صحيحه لا تضاد بين الحديثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A descriptive phrase can add elaboration and praise rather than identify or clarify; attributes of God may also identify because they are truly His attributes, not merely ornaments of praise.
rows.anchor: فقوله لم تزده بيان انها للاطناب والثناء لا للتعريف والتبيين وقيل ان الصفات الجارية على القديم سبحانه المراد بها التعريف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says الذين أسلموا is praise only, since there could be no prophets who were not Muslims, and indirectly reproaches Jews as estranged from the prophets’ religion.
rows.anchor: فهذا الوصف للمدح ليس غير لانه ليس يمكن ان يكون ثمة نبيون غير مسلمين كذا قاله الزمخشري قال واريد بها التعريض باليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the description distinguishes the prophets and honors Islam: their submission to God’s command reaches its highest form, as also in Abraham and Ishmael’s prayer and Joseph’s wish to die Muslim.
rows.anchor: والتحقيق ان هذه الصفة للتمييز وقد اطلق الله وصف الاسلام على الانبياء واتباعهم والأصل في المدح التمييز بين الممدوح وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik gives “the unlettered Prophet” as an adjective that adds clarification; the author questions this because “Messenger of God” is also used of other messengers and is defined by its annexation.
rows.anchor: الثاني لزيادة البيان كذا قاله ابن مالك ومثله بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Messenger of God” is not inherently unique to Muhammad; its frequent use for him is convention, while the Qur’an also applies it to other messengers, including Jesus and Moses.
rows.anchor: قلنا ليس هذا من وضعه بل ذلك من الاستعمال وقد استعمل في غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An adjective can be as definite as or less definite than its noun, but cannot outrank it in definiteness because it is subordinate.
rows.anchor: ثم ان الصفة انما تكون مثل الموصوف أو دونه في التعريف واما ان تكون فوقه فلا لانها على كل حال تابعة والتابع دون المتبوع

words: مِن دَآبَّةٍ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا طَٰٓئِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ
rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkaki takes the modifiers “on earth” and “with its wings” as specifying the genus, supported by the plural “communities like you,” rather than identifying particular individuals.
rows.anchor: هذا معنى ما اشار اليه السكاكي في المفتاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds a reading that the modifiers merely exclude a particular animal farfetched, since a negative indefinite with the exhaustive من is already fully general.
rows.anchor: وحمل بعضهم كلامه على انه انما ذكر الوصف ليعلم ان المراد ليس دابه مخصوصة وهو بعيد لان ذلك معلوم قطعا بدون الوصف لان النكرة المنفية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says these modifiers widen the generality to every creature on earth and every bird in the sky, whose conditions are preserved and affairs attended to.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري ان معنى زيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that “flying” can describe rational beings such as jinn and angels, so “with its wings” specifies the ordinary winged bird intended here.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل ان يقال ان الطيران لما كان يوصف به من يعقل كالجان والملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resumed “you will soon know” suits Shuayb’s repeated appeals and long warning period; the Prophet’s shorter warning is followed by a faʾ that signals the threat’s imminence.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال لما كررت مراجعته لقوم ناسب اختصاص قصته بالاستئناف الذي هو أبلغ في الإنذار والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible explanation is that Shuayb’s people asked the preceding question, making his answer appropriate, whereas the Prophet was not answering a question and no ellipsis fits.
rows.anchor: ولعل قوم شعيب سألوه السؤال المتقدم فأجابهم بهذا الجواب والفاء لا تحسن فيه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the Qur’an uses “forgive you some of your sins” in addresses to unbelievers to distinguish their promise from that made to believers.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري في تفسير سورة إبراهيم

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi objects that if forgiveness is partial, this answer is unnecessary, while if it is not partial, the proposed explanation fails.
rows.anchor: واعترض الإمام فخر الدين بأن هذا

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan asks why the wording differs when both an unbeliever who believes and a believer who repents receive forgiveness; any partial-forgiveness rationale applies to both.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ أثير الدين أبو حيان في تفسيره

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ and others say there is no inversion: the keys weigh down and incline the group carrying them toward collapse.
rows.anchor: وقيل لا قلب فيه والمراد والله أعلم أن المفاتح تنوء بالعصبة أي تميلها من نقلها وقد ذكر هذا الفراء وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن عصفور
rows.claim: Ibn Asfur endorses al-Farisi’s analysis: the intransitive ناء becomes transitive with باء, so the keys make the group lean under their weight; this regular construction is preferable to unlicensed inversion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عصفور والصحيح ما ذهب إليه الفارسي أنها بالنقل ولا قلب والفعل غير متعد فصار متعديا بالباء

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thalab and Ibn al-Sikkit take the phrase as inverted: it means that haste was created from the human.
rows.anchor: خلق العجل من الإنسان قاله ثعلب وابن السكيت

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj cites “man is ever hasty” as support for understanding haste as the intended sense in “created from haste.”
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج ويدل على ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni prefers “created the human from haste,” since people commonly practice and rely on haste; this is stronger in sense and avoids an unlikely inversion.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جنى والأحسن أن يكون تقديره خلق الإنسان من العجلة لكثرة فعله إياه واعتماده له وهو أقوى في المعنى من القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although عجل can mean clay, the author rejects that sense here: “do not ask Me to hasten” and “man is hasty” show that haste is intended, a kind of weakness born of need.
rows.anchor: ولما خفي هذا على بعضهم قال إن العجل هاهنا الطين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some treat the wording about death’s agony arriving with truth as an inversion; the source says Abu Bakr’s reading has this form.
rows.anchor: وهكذا في قراءة أبي بكر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains this as: every matter God has written has an appointed term.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء أي لكل أمر كتبه الله أجل مؤجل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some read “if He intends good for you” as an inversion of “if He intends by you the good,” noting the Arabic idiom for intending good for someone.
rows.anchor: هو من المقلوب أي يريد بك الخير ويقال أراده بالخير وأراد به الخير

rows.speaker: ابن الضائع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Da'iʿ treats the phrase as inverted: Adam truly receives the words, but it is close to say the words met him because the other party sought the encounter too; a reading reverses it.
rows.anchor: وجعل ابن الضائع منه ﴿ فتلقى

rows.speaker: ابن مجاهد
rows.claim: Asked how many Qur’anic occurrences end with إلا غرورا, Ibn Mujahid answers four, in al-Nisa, al-Isra, al-Ahzab, and Fatir.
rows.anchor: سئل ابن مجاهد كم فى القرآن

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i counts four verses beginning with the letter shin and names them: “Month of Ramadan,” “God bears witness,” “grateful for His favor,” and “He prescribed for you of religion.”
rows.anchor: وسئل الكسائى كم فى القرآن آية أولها شين

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i counts two verses ending in shin: “like carded wool” and “For the accustomed security of Quraysh.”
rows.anchor: وسئل كم آية آخرها شين فأجاب اثنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source records five occurrences of حكيم عليم: three in al-An'am, one in al-Hijr, and one in al-Nahl.
rows.anchor: قال خمسة ثلاثة فى الأنعام وفى الحجر واحد وفى النحل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The maximum run of consecutive vowelled letters is eight, occurring between the waw of كوكبا and the ya of رأيت in this verse.
rows.anchor: أكثر ما اجتمع فى كتاب الله من الحروف المتحركة ثمانية

words: حتى يأذن لي أبي أو يحكم الله لي
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other eight-vowel sequence is in this Yusuf verse when the two yaʾs in لي and أبي are vowelled; the source compares it with “We shall strengthen your arm through your brother.”
rows.anchor: على قراءة من حرك الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every successive surah from al-Inshirah to the end of the Qur’an contains all the letters of the Arabic alphabet.
rows.anchor: وفى القرآن سور متواليات كل سورة تجمع حروف المعجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source says one verse contains all the letters of the alphabet, beginning “Muhammad is the Messenger of God.”
rows.anchor: وآية واحدة تجمع حروف المعجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mujadila is the surah in which every verse contains the name of God.
rows.anchor: وسورة كل آية منها فيها اسمه تعالى وهى سورة المجادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Six consecutive verses at the end of al-Hajj each end with two names of God, beginning with ليدخلنهم مدخلا يرضونه.
rows.anchor: وفى الحج ستة آيات متواليات فى آخر كل واحدة منهن اسمان من أسماء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three verses in the Qur’an begin with the phrase قل يا أيها: one addressing people, one addressing the Jews, and one addressing the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وفى القرآن آيات أولها ﴿ قل يا أيها ﴾ ثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source notes two verses beginning يا أيها الإنسان, one asking what deceived the person about the generous Lord and one saying the person labors toward the Lord.
rows.anchor: وفيه ﴿ يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم ﴾ ﴿ يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse يا نوح اهبط بسلام contains sixteen instances of the letter mīm.
rows.anchor: آية فى القرآن فيها ستة عشر ميما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse on deferred debts contains thirty-three instances of the letter mīm.
rows.anchor: وآية فيها ثلاث وثلاثون ميما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inviting hearers to reflect and understand more makes them eager to belong to the praised group of thoughtful people, hastening assent and opening them to guidance.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك استدعاء المخاطب إلى فضل تأمل وزيادة تفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument form called الضمير or التمثيل leaves one premise implicit; “prodigals are brothers of devils” relies on the unstated premise that Satan is ungrateful to his Lord.
rows.anchor: ويكون هذا القول البلاغى ما يسمى الضمير ويسمى التمثيل وأعنى بالضمير أن يضمر بالقول المجادل به البيان أحد حرفيه كقول الفقيه النبيذ مسكر فهو حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted premise can also occur in a conditional argument: since people did not disperse from Muhammad, the observed fact proves that he was not harsh or hard-hearted.
rows.anchor: وقد شهد الحس والعيان انهم ما انفضوا من حوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet’s line about Abdullah illustrates an argument whose omitted premise is brought into view by the stated contrast.
rows.anchor: ومن أحسن ما أبرز فيه هذا المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s confession and plea for forgiveness exemplify rhetoric of winning sympathy and entreating the listener.
rows.anchor: ومثال الاستمالة والاستعطاف قوله تعالى عن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman’s pleading verse moved the “leader of the God-fearing” to say he would not have killed her had he heard it beforehand; another poetic line likewise asks the generous to pardon its speakers.
rows.anchor: وحسبك إمام المتقين حين سمع شعر القائلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The line “We are the writers, and we have erred; pardon us, you noble writers” is another example of entreaty and appeasement.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخر … ونحن الكاتبون وقد أسأنا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When the Ansar felt hurt by the distribution of booty, the Prophet invited them to speak truthfully, reassured them he would not be angered, and honored them for returning with him while others took livestock; he sensed their silence was respect, not inability.
rows.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم للأنصار وقد وجدوا فى نفوسهم قسمة الغنائم فى غيرهم يا معشر الأنصار ألم أجدكم كذا ألم أجدكم كذا ثم قال أجيبونى

rows.speaker: الحليمي
rows.claim: Al-Hulaymi counts avoiding the mixing of one surah with another among the etiquettes of recitation.
rows.anchor: عد الحليمى من الآداب ترك خلط سورة بسورة

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says the Qur’an’s arrangement came through the Prophet from Gabriel, so readers should follow the transmitted, agreed order.
rows.anchor: قال البيهقى وأحسن ما يحتج به أن يقال إن هذا التأليف لكتاب الله مأخوذ من جهة النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وأخذه عن جبريل

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin says God’s arrangement is better than people’s arrangement.
rows.anchor: وقد قال ابن سيرين تأليف الله خير من تأليفكم

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr transmits consensus against reciting one verse from each of several surahs in alternation.
rows.anchor: ونقل القاضى أبو بكر الإجماع على عدم جواز قراءة آية آية من كل سورة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says the Prophet heard Abu Bakr reciting softly, Umar loudly, and Bilal mixing passages from different surahs; he said they were all correct.
rows.anchor: من حديث أبى هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر بأبى بكر وهو يقرأ

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd’s version adds that Bilal was told to read a surah in its order, or to carry it through when reciting it.
rows.anchor: وفى رواية لأبى عبيد فى فضائل القرآن قال بلال أخلط الطيب بالطيب فقال اقرأ السورة على وجهها أو قال على نحوها

rows.speaker: خالد بن الوليد
rows.claim: Khalid ibn al-Walid once led prayer using passages from several surahs, then explained that jihad had kept him from learning the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وروى عن خالد بن الوليد أنه أم الناس فقرأ من سور شتى ثم التفت إلى الناس حين انصرف فقال شغلنى الجهاد عن تعلم القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd initially says the practice is disliked, citing the Prophet’s apparent disapproval of Bilal, Khalid’s apology, and Ibn Sirin’s dislike; he also notes a stronger report in which the Prophet says all the recitations are good.
rows.anchor: ثم قال أبو عبيد الأمر عندنا على الكراهة فى قراءة القراء هذه الآيات المختلفة كما أنكر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على بلال

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd judges the version “all of that is good” more reliable and more consonant with the transmission of scholars.
rows.anchor: ثم قال إن بعضهم روى حديث بلال وفيه فقال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم كل ذلك حسن وهو أثبت وأشبه بنقل العلماء

rows.speaker: الحكيم الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi compares Bilal to a bee that eats sweet and sour fruit yet produces healing, unlike birds that select only what tastes sweet.
rows.anchor: ورواه الحكيم الترمذى فى نوادر الأصول وزاد مثل بلال كمثل نحلة غدت تأكل من الحلو والمر ثم يصير حلوا كله

rows.speaker: الحكيم الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi says Bilal sought mercy verses and descriptions of Paradise, but the Prophet directed him to the revealed surah order: God mixed themes to meet people’s needs and keep hearts from weariness.
rows.anchor: فبلال رضى الله عنه كان يقصد آيات الرحمة وصفات الجنة فأمره أن يقرأ السورة على نحوها كما جاءت ممتزجة كما أنزل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحكيم الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi says الرحمن suits the hearts facing the terror of the Day of Judgment and softens their fear; a harsher divine name such as العزيز or الجبار would make their hearts burst.
rows.anchor: ورواه الحكيم الترمذى فى نوادر الأصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “A surah We have sent down,” the omitted element may be supplied as “a surah among what We revealed to you” or as “this is a surah.”
rows.anchor: إما أن يقدر فيما أوحينا إليك سورة أو هذه سورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians commonly allow agent omission in three settings: a passive verb, a verbal noun with no expressed or implicit agent, and where the agent would meet a following word beginning with a silent letter.
rows.anchor: المشهور امتناعه إلا في ثلاثة مواضع أحدها إذا بنى الفعل للمفعول ثانيها في المصدر إذا لم يذكر معه الفاعل مظهرا

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa’i allows an unexpressed agent whenever context identifies it: the soul reaches the collarbones, the sun disappears, punishment descends, or a messenger comes to Solomon.
rows.anchor: وجوز الكسائي حذفه مطلقا إذا ما وجد ما يدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s correction is that the agent in these examples is implicit, not deleted; he distinguishes the two grammatical analyses.
rows.anchor: والحق أنه في المذكورات مضمر لا محذوف وقد سبق الفرق بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the passive “the matter about which you inquire has been decreed,” the agent is omitted to magnify the one who decreed it.
rows.anchor: إذ كان الذي قضاه عظيم القدر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the passive wording “what was sent down to you” better conveys the sender’s greatness than the anomalous active reading, especially for acts only God can perform.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري في كشافه القديم

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni’s criterion for omitting a known agent is that the point is to report the action’s occurrence on its object, not to identify its doer.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جنى وضابطه أن يكون الغرض إنما هو الإعلام بوقوع الفعل بالمفعول ولا غرض في إبانة الفاعل من هو
